findings.title: Invoice effective HSN lookup calls a method absent from the frontend service and API routes

evidence.note: API only rate list and create
Catch silently substitutes legacy Item-master HSN
Underlying application service does support effective classification

findings.impact: Current call fails synchronously inside the try and falls back to raw item HSN. Effective-dated/category-default/item-override classification is not actually resolved by this UI. The underlying application logic exists, but is not exposed through the reviewed controller/client service.
findings.recommendation: Choose and clearly present the supported classification source. If effective mapping is required, expose/review its API and frontend method, provide permission-aware mapping maintenance, show fallback reason, and refresh on invoice-date changes. Also guard row autofill by stable row and current Item ID before asynchronous writes.
findings.acceptance: No nonexistent service call; visible HSN source accurately reflects actual lookup. Item override/category default/effective date/legacy fallback each behave explicitly. Delayed row requests cannot overwrite a different current selection.
findings.correction: An initial audit hypothesis described a current async overwrite race. Backend cross-check showed this missing service call prevents the normal awaited branch; the current concrete finding is silent fallback, while stale-row protection remains a requirement when wiring the async path.

findings.title: First-200 static dropdowns hide valid masters and records
findings.impact: As data grows, users cannot find records outside downloaded page, and newly created records may still be absent after a refresh.
findings.recommendation: Remote debounced search with paging and exact by-ID hydration for selected/inactive historical values; expose loading/retry; retain newly created result immediately.
findings.acceptance: Records 201+ can be found and selected in all affected forms; editing historical documents preserves selected inactive records.

findings.title: Supplier changes do not clear/revalidate existing allocations and bill requests can race

evidence.note: Supplier watcher only starts bill load
Async bill load lacks request identity guard

findings.impact: Old supplier bill allocations can remain attached in the form or stale results can appear after quick changes. Server may reject; source review cannot claim incorrect database acceptance.
findings.recommendation: Clear/review allocations when changing supplier, cancel/discard stale bills requests, disable allocation editing until correct bills load; suggest oldest-first allocations and show remaining/unallocated payment.
findings.acceptance: Changing A to B never leaves A bills selected or shown; payment can be split across correct unpaid bills, with total and unallocated amount clear.

findings.title: Return against bill asks operator to repeat supplier and line information
findings.impact: Manual linkage and re-entry invite mismatched supplier/item/original line selection and slow returns.
findings.recommendation: Add Return against this bill/receipt action that preloads authoritative original lines, supplier and remaining returnable quantities; retain explicitly separate financial versus physical-return steps.
findings.acceptance: Operator selects source and quantities, not repeat supplier/items; original IDs retained; excess return disabled with explanation.

findings.title: Purchase detail actions ignore document state
findings.impact: Confirmed/cancelled documents still offer actions the server may reject; creates failed clicks and uncertainty. Contrast: InvoiceDetailPage gates draft/confirmed actions.
findings.recommendation: Use authoritative allowedActions or explicit shared state rules; put one valid next action first and explain read-only/blocked reasons.
findings.acceptance: Draft/sent/received/confirmed/cancelled states expose only permitted transitions; server rejection retains record and gives next step.

findings.title: Sales and purchase page forms collapse API validation into toast
findings.impact: Client validation can highlight fields, but business/server validation may leave the operator unable to identify which row or field to fix.
findings.recommendation: Map safe server field errors onto React Hook Form fields/rows, add persistent summary with jump-to-first-invalid, preserve all entered values and mark uncertain submissions for reconciliation.
findings.acceptance: Duplicate supplier reference, invalid original-line link, insufficient stock or stale version gives persistent actionable field/record feedback.

findings.title: Long forms navigate away without unsaved-change protection
findings.impact: Multi-line transactions and party details can be lost on accidental Back/Cancel/route change. Global rg found no useBlocker/beforeunload guard for these forms.
findings.recommendation: Dirty-form guard across page and modal paths, returnTo/list-context restoration, safe local draft only with user/company isolation and explicit clear-after-save.
findings.acceptance: Leaving changed form requires discard/continue choice; successful save clears guard; returning to list preserves filters and highlights saved record.

findings.title: GST issuance workflow is explicitly incomplete
findings.impact: Existing GST views inspect/reconcile existing records; they cannot be represented as complete issue-to-government workflow.
findings.recommendation: Present role-aware readiness checklist and concrete owner/blocking reason; use invoice-led links and real document register APIs; implement issuance only with verified backend/provider capability and duplicate protection.
findings.acceptance: User can tell available versus unavailable actions without relying on disabled-button hover; successful issue/retry/cancel tested only once genuine backend/provider integration exists.

findings.title: Item manufacturing uses UTC calendar date while newer workflows use company business date

evidence.note: Applicable BOM lookup uses UTC today
New document date uses verified company business date

findings.impact: Around India midnight UTC and company-day differences, selected effective BOM or default production date can differ between entry paths.
findings.recommendation: Use same verified business-date runtime and explicit unavailable-date/manual-entry behavior for BOM applicability and production forms.
findings.acceptance: Before/after midnight and backdated company calendar produce the same applicable BOM/default date across item production and production orders.

findings.title: Two production entry paths coexist inside and outside Item master

evidence.note: New workflow item configuration also embedded

findings.impact: Operator can confuse master setup, legacy one-shot manufacture and newer order/daily/board workflow.

findings.title: Document and cash ledgers require wide horizontal tables
findings.impact: Overflow prevents clipping but phone users must pan repeatedly between item/quantity/price/actions.
findings.recommendation: Retain fast desktop sheet, add responsive line cards/drawer editor with item and totals pinned; desktop keyboard navigation and paste only after row validation.
findings.acceptance: At 360px width operator can identify item, edit quantity and save with visible row context and no page-level horizontal pan.

findings.title: GST setup/support asks operators to know internal IDs and exact strings

evidence.note: Company ID/branch ID and free status
Exact API type and registration ID

findings.title: Item stock controls rewrite decimal strings via JavaScript Number

evidence.note: Opening stock payload uses numeric conversion

findings.impact: Large/high-precision stock values can visibly change on blur before save. Backend range/precision was not validated during this audit.
findings.recommendation: Apply canonical decimal-string quantity handling with documented scale/range and explicit rounding; show entered value and reject excess precision rather than silently rewriting.

findings.title: Expense category and daily cash workflows are separate families without visible origin guidance
findings.impact: An operator can reasonably ask whether to record the same cash cost under Expenses, My Wallet or Transactions. No claim that backend duplicates balances: automatic cross-module posting was not traced.
findings.recommendation: Document one authoritative expense-entry path, show source/link on resulting cash movement, and make manual versus automatic posting clear; audit backend posting ownership before adding automation.

findings.title: Rojmel transaction and wallet labels disagree with backend enums

evidence.note: Filter options consume numeric enum values

findings.impact: Ledger badges and filters can call opening balances adjustments, adjustment-in opening balances and adjustment-out Other. Wallet creation/filters can label a PettyCash choice Bank. Backend status1 Posted is also shown as Active.
findings.recommendation: Use backend canonical enum contract to generate shared labels/options, explicitly distinguish adjustment directions and Posted status, and apply consistently to filters/badges/report columns.
findings.acceptance: Known backend transaction types1–7 and wallet types1–5 display and filter with matching meaning; create wallet choice stores the advertised backend type; old rows remain correctly classified.

findings.title: Party type is omitted from create/edit payload even though grouped customer/supplier flows depend on it

evidence.note: Command-field allowlist has no partyType through line81
Payload built only from supplied fields

findings.impact: Quick-create labeled Customer or Supplier omits its role and backend defaults Both. Updating an existing typed party can also reset its type to Both under the current command default; database acceptance/state was not exercised.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit Customer/Supplier/Both field; preselect role from originating transaction and preserve existing role on edit; keep server validation aligned and clarify one shared party record can serve both.
findings.acceptance: Create Customer and Supplier yields intended type, edit preserves role unless deliberately changed, and Both appears in both document lookups.

findings.title: Party setting flags are persisted without a connected form or print behavior

evidence.note: Settings loaded only for settings editor
Party fields are fixed command fields
Party record has standard fields, no additional-field values

findings.impact: Saving flags such as shipping/grouping/custom fields can appear to enable a behavior that the reviewed frontend form/print does not read. Source search found flag names only in settings schema/persistence; runtime effects were not tested.
findings.recommendation: Declare actual support of each setting and wire supported flags through to consumers with preview. Keep future loyalty/reminder/custom-field options visibly unavailable until data and behavior are implemented.
findings.acceptance: Each exposed setting has an observable defined effect, persists on reload and is tested at its consuming form/print; unsupported options clearly state prerequisite.

strengths.description: Canonical masters and permission-aware inline create already reduce navigation during transaction entry.
Party GSTIN verification, reviewed autofill and same-as-billing shipping already remove manual work.
BOMs retain version/effective dates/components; production post explains stock impact and timeout recovery.
Physical procurement retains original receipt/version/disposition and separates receipt stock from financial bill linkage.
Rojmel protects self-wallet scope, explains transfer neutrality and requires reasoned reversal.
GST mutations require reconciled matching active context and uncertain outcomes are blocked pending reconciliation; logs avoid raw secrets.

limitations: Source review of actual pages, embedded sections/modals, services and selected backend contracts. No live browser proof, database writes, backend starts, or provider calls performed by this sub-audit.
No claim of exhaustive runtime QA or complete production readiness. Source-confirmed missing UI checks describe possible user-facing outcomes; backend may reject unsafe requests.
Rojmel category lookup is implemented; no category maintenance UI/API was found in this reviewed family. This is a read lookup family rather than an asserted missing sidebar master.
Manufacturing Work Centre/Operation/routing internals and global Reports/navigation are delegated elsewhere. Item embedded configuration and commerce integration boundaries were included here.

Inventory categories and expense categories are flat canonical masters; no parent/child hierarchy was found in their actual form schemas. Party group filters are classifications rather than standalone group master CRUD.
Automatic ledger/cash posting ownership across Expenses, Supplier Payments and Rojmel was not fully traced; C15 intentionally calls for an ownership audit before any automation change.

Nested backend cross-check distinguishes persistence/application-only HSN families from actual exposed API/client functionality. Current fixed enums were checked against local backend source; source code is evidence, not a substitute for live response verification.

backendCrossCheck.result: Canonical party CRUD/status/export and separate settings GET/PUT exist. PartyType omission and settings consumption gaps documented C17/C18.

Canonical master CRUD exists, categories/units are flat and fields match their UI. Item HSN legacy field and procurement classification are actual Item request members. Manufacturing BOM/routing/packaging cross-check is covered by operations audit.

Catalog/category defaults/item overrides/effective resolver application methods and DTOs exist, but API controller and frontend service expose only rate versions. Added four explicit unavailable frontend workflow rows; C01 identifies dangling invoice method.

Category GET lookup and enum Income/Expense/Both match frontend; no category-maintenance controller in reviewed Rojmel family. Wallet CRUD is present. Transaction/wallet enums mismatch UI (C16). These are fixed enumerations, not missing CRUD masters.
Create/list/get/update/confirm/cancel plus payments POST/GET exist. Print template choice lives in client preview; no claim of separate server template master.

Expense categories full CRUD; bills/order/returns/supplier payments/expenses APIs exist. Supplier payment allocation and return original bill-line ID are real DTO child fields. No separate extra configuration master inferred from static UI enums.
Frontend actual receipt/return/credit/promise/link flows inspected. Backend physical controllers are separate from financial document CRUD, preserving ownership boundary.
